How Much to Charge for Embroidered Hats: Full Cap Order Breakdown

Walk through a 24-cap order with blank hat markup and setup fees end to end, and build your own cap quote in the calculator below.

Jump to calculator

What Makes Pricing Embroidered Hats Different

Custom embroidered hats are one of the most frequent repeat orders for both small commercial shops and home multi-needle embroiderers. Unlike flat polo shirts or tote bags, structured caps are stitched on a curved cap driver and cap frame, require tear-away cap backing, and are almost always sold as a complete package where the shop supplies the blank hats.

To quote an embroidered hat order accurately without losing margin on the blank headwear, your calculation needs to keep three numbers distinct:

  1. The per-cap decoration price (based on stitch count, hooping fee, extra colors, quantity break discount, and your per-piece minimum).
  2. The marked-up blank cap price (your wholesale cap cost multiplied by 1 + garment markup).
  3. Any one-time setup or digitizing fee added to the order total after multiplying the per-piece price by the hat quantity.

Let's price a complete 24-cap order end to end using Worked Example 2 from our pricing formula. Note that the starting values used below ($1.50 per 1,000 stitches, $1.00 per-piece fee, $5.00 minimum, 40% garment markup, and 650 stitches per minute) are editable placeholders—change them in the rate panel above to match your shop's cap rates.

Worked Example 2: 24 Custom Caps with Blank Hat Markup and Setup Fee

Suppose a contractor orders 24 caps featuring an 8,000-stitch front logo in 3 thread colors (which means 2 color changes). You purchase the blank caps wholesale for $4.50 each, apply a 40% garment markup, and charge a $25.00 one-time setup fee to prepare and test the cap file.

1. Calculate the Per-Cap Decoration Price

First, compute the base decoration charge from the stitch count and per-piece handling fee:

  • Stitch charge: (8,000 ÷ 1,000) × $1.50 = 8 × $1.50 = $12.00
  • Per-piece hooping/handling fee: $1.00
  • Extra colors: 3 colors is within the 6 included colors, so $0.00 extra-color fee.
  • Base decoration price: $12.00 + $1.00 = $13.00 per cap.

Next, apply the quantity break for 24 caps. In the starting break schedule (1–11: 0%, 12–23: 5%, 24–47: 10%, 48–143: 15%, 144+: 20%), 24 caps qualify for the 10% break:

  • Discounted decoration: $13.00 × (1 − 0.10) = $11.70 per cap.
  • Minimum check: $11.70 is above the $5.00 per-piece minimum, so decoration remains $11.70.

2. Add the Blank Cap Cost and Markup

When you supply the blank hats, you tie up cash purchasing inventory, pay incoming shipping, and absorb the risk of an occasional cap getting damaged during hooping or needle deflection on a thick center seam. Marking up the blank garment covers that risk and inventory cost:

garment price per piece = garment cost × (1 + garment markup)

For a $4.50 blank cap at a 40% (0.40) markup:

  • Marked-up cap price: $4.50 × 1.40 = $6.30 per cap (providing $1.80 of garment margin per cap, or $43.20 across 24 caps).
  • Combined per-piece price: $11.70 decoration + $6.30 cap = $18.00 per cap (rounded half up to the cent before multiplying by quantity).

3. Multiply by Quantity and Add the One-Time Setup Fee

Now multiply the rounded $18.00 per-cap price by 24 caps and add the one-time $25.00 setup fee:

  • 24 embroidered caps at $18.00 each: $18.00 × 24 = $432.00
  • One-time setup fee: $25.00
  • Order total: $432.00 + $25.00 = $457.00

Compare that side by side with Worked Example 1, where the customer supplied the 24 caps with no setup fee:

  • Customer supplies caps, $0 setup (Worked Example 1): $11.70/cap · $280.80 order total
  • Shop supplies $4.50 caps at 40% markup + $25 setup (Worked Example 2): $18.00/cap · $457.00 order total

Full Quantity Price Table for This Cap Order

Contractors and sports teams frequently ask, "What if we order 12 hats now, or bump the order to 48 hats?" Using the exact Worked Example 2 inputs (8,000 stitches, 3 colors, $4.50 blank cap at 40% markup = $6.30, plus $25.00 one-time setup fee), here is every quantity break tier:

  • 1–11 caps (0% break): $13.00 decoration + $6.30 cap = $19.30/cap (1 cap with $25 setup = $44.30; 11 caps with $25 setup = $237.30)
  • 12–23 caps (5% break): $12.35 decoration + $6.30 cap = $18.65/cap (12 caps with $25 setup = $248.80)
  • 24–47 caps (10% break): $11.70 decoration + $6.30 cap = $18.00/cap (24 caps with $25 setup = $457.00)
  • 48–143 caps (15% break): $11.05 decoration + $6.30 cap = $17.35/cap (48 caps with $25 setup = $857.80)
  • 144+ caps (20% break): $10.40 decoration + $6.30 cap = $16.70/cap (144 caps with $25 setup = $2,429.80)

Note that the quantity break discount applies only to the decoration portion of the price ($13.00 down to $10.40), while the marked-up blank cap remains $6.30 unless your blank supplier gives you a case-lot discount that you choose to enter in the blank garment cost field.

Adjusting Machine Speed and Hooping Time for Caps

Many shops run caps slightly slower than flat garments to reduce needle deflection on center seams and buckram panels. At the starting speed of 650 stitches per minute with 2 color changes (30 seconds each) and 1.0 minute of cap framing, each cap takes 14.31 minutes and earns an effective decoration hourly rate of $49.06/hr at 24 pieces. If you run caps at 550 stitches per minute and spend 1.5 minutes clamping each cap on the gauge, enter those numbers in Shop Rate Settings & Machine Speed above: machine time shifts to 17.05 minutes per cap ($41.17/hr), showing you immediately if you should increase your per-piece fee for hats.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does the quantity break discount reduce my blank hat markup?

No. In the calculator's formula, quantity break discounts apply only to the decoration price. Your blank garment cost and garment markup percentage stay intact across all quantity tiers.

How do I price a hat that has both a front logo and a small back-arch text design?

Because a front logo and a back-arch design require two separate hoopings on the cap frame, you can either run a separate quote for each placement or combine the stitch counts and increase the per-piece hooping fee and hooping minutes to reflect the second framing.

Can I upload my cap DST file directly into this page?

Yes. Drop your cap .dst or .pes file into the box at the top of this page to read the exact stitch count, color changes, and dimensions, then uncheck "Customer supplies garment" to enter your blank hat cost.
